title: The River Takes Its Skin

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Stone comes on and the river puts on its skin and gives no account of the cold. The kiln keeps its breath in fours. The slate keeps one in twelve. A house that cannot read goes on keeping what it cannot pay for.
epigraph.attribution: A firing-yard saying of Low Kiln, at the coming in of Stone

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of three hundred and sixty to three hundred and sixty-two days, six months and one hundred and eighty to one hundred and eighty-two days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. No present-tense break and no tagged memory: as in chapters 25 through 102 the old life is carried by the surgeon's register alone. Each morning the register takes the body in its old order — the stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear with its corner standing a hair off the wool, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, as at the end of a line written out for it, with neither an order to go farther nor an order to go away; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform — and reads the world as a trauma bay is read, by the small sounds first because the small sounds do not lie. He knows the composed face is not composure, knows a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed from outside and slowly, never rubbed, never set too near the fire; he knows the infant's want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle is louder than the surgeon's knowing, and neither wins, and the argument is the work. The carried fire keeps four low pulls with its fifth unpaid through three hundred and sixty, sixty-one and sixty-two days and its payer unnamed; the boards keep four nails on the near one, four on the next and a thumb-width knot; the river that went water over water under the finger's-width door goes under its winter skin in these three days, a covering put on by the cold and entered nowhere. Six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among with the seventh place empty; the heard bell stays in its square beside the told bell, four, four and a gap. Nine arithmetics of the year stand behind one unsigned figure — nine are nine and not one account — with all three Ash subtractions locked and unread in Berr Clay's box up the clay road, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space, and no doctrine standing out of nine. The deep-winter month in which he was born comes on without a boundary drawn and neither habit of naming the months is corrected; its first firing stands beyond the close and unbrought, the first birthday on Stone 7 (Day 366) further still and the Hearth Drawing of Stone 12 (Day 371) further still, and none is named to him under any roof. Nothing is opened, joined by a standing hand, named, called, paid or ended.
places: the flat stone by the well

scenes.title: Stone Comes On
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, the chapter's only \dropcap and its first \daymark{360}{Stone 1, Firstday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof into the first light of an ordinary tending day with no market, Cross or bell, no collector on the clay road and no runner on any road. Open on the hand laid down against the fold on answer 294 as a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking. No recap: nothing from Ash 28, 29 or 30 crosses as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment — the ninth reading bought no lesson under this roof and the nine arithmetics stand as nine and not one account. Carry 294 honest answers on the sixth place, six hearings with the seventh place empty, the heard bell beside the told with four, four and a gap, nine hands with no tenth, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and the loan uncalled, five held objects with the pot-crack resting beside them and the hand-at-the-sill breath beside that and the holding of Ash 26 beside all, burned slate at five, shut-room tellings at two, well-saying at four shapings, row at five askings, and the Ash 5 joining, Ash 17 direction and Ash 23 direction apart with a finger between every pair, still gathering and unspent. Count 359 → 360 exact, six months and one hundred and seventy-nine → one hundred and eighty days told by nobody (T071/T072): six months stand exactly at the close of this day and nobody speaks the number or calls it a threshold, and the boy keeps it exactly without expecting to be told, which is not the same as not wanting it. The carried fire's fifth unpaid 360 days with its payer unnamed (T088); Garl's name unspoken 360 days (T009/T013/T092). Body inventory in the surgeon's old order: crust stiff and leathery two inches off with its corner a hair off the wool, empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold stopping at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform, composed face not composure, a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed slowly from outside; the infant's louder want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrelling without verdict, both true, neither winning (T060/T086). Hearth grammar at both ends of the morning's opening, beat for beat: fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, *The house will keep it* where another woman would say I, a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal tally stays unread, lips on a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar standing cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crosses the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline showing, dressed grain turned under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and no figure or handful, pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed (T058/T079/T100, T077). Widow's mark untouched — a morning and a hearth are not openings; six openings in six months are six and not a rule, the sixth held at the kiln mouth on Ash 2 without a name, no seventh made due, and the kiln standing cold these three mornings with its first firing of Stone still beyond the close (T058/T079). The Ash ridge along the skirting board is thicker in the dark month's cold and unswept; the boy files the thickness as weather entered nowhere, not an eighth opening, a cause or a payment (T009/T013/T092). In the small hours the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note under the finger's-width door, takes a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing, comes straight down and lays itself back against the fold — answer 295: exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across none of the held objects (T061/T082). Stone comes on without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming its months corrected; the month carries both names the way a pot carries two handles and is none the worse. Its first firing, the birthday on Stone 7 and the Drawing on Stone 12 stand beyond the close as dates and are not brought into a day that has not earned them.

scenes.title: The River Takes Its Skin
scenes.synopsis: Second entry, no new dated heading: the afternoon of Stone 1 through the going of the light and the bed, then the small hours. THIS SCENE HOLDS THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE (T083/T085 and T078 advanced and NOT paid). Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail; Garl in objects. Walk-ons only: the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with kindling, two fence-menders. No Ilva, no Berr, no Hessa on any road, no runner, no collector, no market, Cross or bell, no green-mouthed woman or foundling sighting, and no ownerless voice over the boards — the Ash 5 joining, Ash 17 direction and Ash 23 direction stand where they were put and do not repeat and buy no lesson. Sella carries him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire to be banked against their coming back, never to the basket, and goes wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and no number, widest around the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Three coverings stay weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair and no fourth likeness made a cause: the gone white frost on the well's north lip, the skin on the trough, the silt-clouded plate of ice on its flat stone out of the path of feet (T083/T085). **The one change: in the afternoon the river's note under the finger's-width door comes no longer water over water in the open but low under a skin — \place{the Ilm} has taken its winter ice from bank to bank.** A man come down from Cold Acre says the river has gone under and, asked what the ice will cost, tells the questioner to ask the weather, which laid it on and will take it off; no slate is opened and no figure comes (T077). The boy files the new note on a place of its own beside water-over-water, which stays where it was put: a covering put on by the cold and taken off by the cold, entered nowhere, expressly not a sixth low thing standing up as a rule, not a hearing, not a seventh of the full note, not a fourth of the three coverings (each of which stays on its own place with a finger between), not a sign, a lesson, a cause, a payment or a payer. Advanced and not paid; it plants toward the deep winter, the kiln's first firing on Stone 5, the birthday on Stone 7 and the Drawing on Stone 12 without bringing any of them into this day. Dressed grain is turned once under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child, no figure, no handful; hunts and repairs stay directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, never figures — hare to the weather, cracked jar to a pot that says nothing, *Yes, house* to early and late with the late kept because it puts off the paying (T077). At the kindling Tarn keeps six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged collector sentence, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, checks the Bone 26 thumb's resting and the Ash 14 held breath and finds each where put and not made again, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, Seed 16 breath unspent and loan uncalled, his stroke over the bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076/T006). Jorra comes through the finger's-width door with meal-fine grey slate dust white in a fist-crease, parts dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel before any person (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*) and tells a pot *You'll do*, knows the full note three turns ahead and withholds it, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence — one iron with two bites, the holding and the taking — without leaving the extra interval of Ash 26 a second time, that holding gathered once and not spent where nobody would enter it (T062/T035/T031). At the going of the light Sella sets him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, her hand resting the half-beat longer than the setting needed, and leaves the thread frozen and unwiped; she says nothing of where they had been; the widow's mark stays untouched because an afternoon and a going of the light are not openings. In the small hours the hand goes up an inch, takes a small intake, holds the interval whole on the river's finishing — now under its skin — and lays itself back against the fold — answer 296, exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Ninth Hand at the Well

The three coverings stay weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair and no fourth likeness made a cause, and the newly iced river stays a covering on its own place beside water-over-water and is not joined to them (T083/T085). Dressed grain lies covered and unfigured with no handful lifted, her fingers in and out without closing (T077). I keep the count, not the account* — and puts her flat hand once more on the sleeve and goes back to the pail, nobody turning twice. **The boy takes the order of reaching apart as a surgeon takes a field apart and files it as the ninth record-first hand on a place of its own with a finger between it and Hessa Rale's eighth, filing no tenth** (T080 advanced and not paid); he makes no reader of her own keeping and joins her to none, and she is expressly not the speaker of any voice. At the kindling Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged collector sentence, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, checks the Ash 14 held breath and the Bone 26 thumb's resting and finds each where put and not made again, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, Seed 16 breath unspent and loan uncalled (T036/T076/T006). In the small hours the hand goes up an inch, takes a small intake, holds the interval whole on the river's finishing under the ice, comes straight down — answer 298, exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082).

scenes.title: Three Hundred Answers
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: the afternoon of Stone 3 at the Clay Yard's seven places, the yard well and flat stone, the rack end, the kindling, the flagstones, the wheel-shed edge and damper, then the going of the light, the hearth, pot board, loaf shelf, bed, boards and towel. The whole file comes out on the towel at the head of the bed as instruments come out on a towel and is checked and left as it lay: **300 honest answers stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power, and not one stands up and calls itself a doctrine**; six hearings of the full note beside and never among with the seventh place empty, the sixth the small flat knock out of a woman as the men lifted her, filed where a thing out of a person must go; heard bell beside told, four, four and a gap; nine record-first hands with no tenth (Ilva's ninth, Hessa's eighth); nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and the loan uncalled; five held objects with the pot-crack resting, the hand-at-the-sill breath and the holding of Ash 26 beside them, none a sixth, seventh or eighth; burned slate at five with shut-room tellings at two, well-saying at four shapings and row at five askings; the Ash 5 joining, Ash 17 direction and Ash 23 direction held apart with a finger between every pair, advanced and not paid; nine arithmetics of the year behind one unsigned figure, nine are nine and not one account, one in twelve printed and unchallenged, figure read not figure paid, no signature on the space, both of Ash's subtractions riding locked and unread up the clay road in Berr's box with the key gone up in a coat pocket, the finding on a place of its own with no payer and no doctrine standing out of nine; the river-under-skin keeping of Stone 1 on its own place beside water-over-water, not a fourth likeness, not a sixth low thing, not a hearing, advanced and not paid (T061/T082, T083/T085, T078, T080, T015/T041/T047, T035/T031/T065/T095 and T101).
